_doc: Investment-cost model for healthcare_provider, grounded in the real playbook config (config/playbooks/healthcare_provider.json, 4 of 4 covered) and the real pillar catalog (config/healthcare_provider_kpi_catalog.json). This vertical's pillar taxonomy (Patient Outcomes / Operational Efficiency / Provider Satisfaction / Compliance & Risk) has NO revenue-adjacent pillar at all — not just no growth pillar (already an established finding: see this catalog's own pillar_roles_notes and power_of_1.json's attribution map), but no 'protect revenue' pillar either. commercial_pressure_save (a renewal-save play) and expansion_intent_handoff (a growth play) both get real cost figures below since cost doesn't depend on a pillar mapping, but neither targets a pillar — this vertical tracks revenue protection and revenue growth as raw dollars, never through a health pillar, for both directions alike. Companion to config/economics/healthcare_provider.json. Same {value, basis} discipline as config/investment/saas_premium.json.

csm_hourly_cost.basis: assumed: blended fully-loaded CSM/CS-ops hourly cost, same figure as every other vertical's file — CSM cost doesn't vary by vertical the way retention sensitivity does (config/investment/saas_premium.json's own basis sentence).

_playbooks_doc: Grounded in config/playbooks/healthcare_provider.json's 4 real playbooks. Three of the four (rollout_stall_recovery, commercial_pressure_save, expansion_intent_handoff) resolve to no pillar at all through power_of_1.json's attribution map crossed with this catalog's pillar_roles ({'compliance': 'P4'} only) — a mechanically-confirmed gap, not a guess (verified by direct cross-reference, 2026-09-07). The fourth (escalation_clinical_response) is targeted to P3 by name-level reasoning (its infra_incident trigger role is an EHR/clinical-systems outage, and P3-KPI2 is literally 'EHR System Uptime'), the same style of judgment call saas_premium's own escalation_exec_response makes for CSAT (P3) despite an identical mechanical gap there.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: clinical-ops incident triage + an exec-to-exec call with hospital IT/clinical-ops leadership + resolution follow-through + a wrap-up communication, 'escalate' action_class

estimated_cost_per_execution.basis: assumed: estimated_csm_hours (assumed) x csm_hourly_cost (assumed) — both links assumed, so the product is assumed, not derived

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.basis: assumed: informal CS-leadership estimate for EHR-uptime/clinical-ops recovery's effect on P3 (Provider Satisfaction); no healthcare_provider tenant yet has >=5 closed instances of this playbook with both a measured lift and a revenue outcome

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: a rollout/adoption audit + a multi-stakeholder alignment call (clinical staff, IT, project sponsor) + a revised project-plan follow-up, 'schedule' action_class — a stalled hospital implementation typically needs more stakeholder coordination than a single renewal conversation, hence above the 4hr schedule baseline used elsewhere in this file family

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: this playbook's trigger role (delivery_stall) resolves to the 'adoption' pillar_role in power_of_1.json's attribution map, but this catalog has no 'adoption' pillar at all (Patient Outcomes / Operational Efficiency / Provider Satisfaction / Compliance & Risk — none play that role; see the catalog's own pillar_roles_notes). No pillar to attribute a health-point lift to. Real, mechanically-confirmed, not guessed.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: a budget-pressure conversation with hospital procurement/finance + a follow-up, 'schedule' action_class

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: this playbook's trigger role (commercial_pressure) resolves to the 'revenue' pillar_role, and this catalog has no revenue-adjacent pillar at all (see the file-level _doc above) — no pillar to attribute a health-point lift to, same reasoning as rollout_stall_recovery.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: qualify the signal + warm handoff to sales, 'notify' action_class — the lightest-touch playbook in this catalog

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: double gap: this playbook's expected_outcome is expansion revenue, not a health-score lift (same shape as saas_premium's expansion_intent_handoff), AND its trigger role has no pillar in this catalog at all (see the file-level _doc above) — this vertical genuinely has no growth pillar, an established finding this project treats as correct, not something to force a parallel structure onto.

_pillars_doc: Pillar-level cost rolls up from the playbooks that target it. A pillar with no targeting playbook is shown as not_covered, not guessed. Coverage here is sparser than every other vertical (1 of 4 pillars, vs. 3-5 of 5-6 pillars elsewhere) — a real finding grounded in this vertical's real playbook catalog, not an authoring gap: see the file-level _doc and _playbooks_doc above.

P1.name: Patient Outcomes
P1.note: no playbook in config/playbooks/healthcare_provider.json targets a signal role that maps to Patient Outcomes; none of the 4 real playbooks are clinical-outcome-triggered (they fire on escalation/infra_incident, delivery_stall, commercial_pressure, expansion_intent — operational and commercial signals, not clinical ones)

P2.name: Operational Efficiency
P2.note: rollout_stall_recovery is the closest conceptual fit (a stalled implementation blocks the operational-efficiency gains the system was meant to deliver) but none of P2's three KPIs (Bed Utilization Rate, Average Wait Time, Staff-to-Patient Ratio) specifically measures rollout completeness, so no claim is made here — left not_covered rather than forced onto a KPI it doesn't cleanly move

P3.name: Provider Satisfaction
P3.note: one playbook covers this pillar, targeting EHR System Uptime (P3-KPI2) specifically — a clinical-systems incident is escalated precisely because it threatens EHR uptime. Provider NPS (P3-KPI1) is also impact:high in the catalog but no playbook names it directly yet — covered at pillar level only, same pattern as saas_premium's P3-KPI3 (NPS) note

P4.name: Compliance & Risk
P4.note: no playbook in config/playbooks/healthcare_provider.json targets the 'compliance' role this pillar plays (the only role this catalog's pillar_roles maps at all) — none of the 4 real playbooks fire on a compliance signal. Absent, not guessed.

_kpis_doc: KPI-level entries exist only for KPIs a playbook actually names in targets_kpis.

P3-KPI2.name: EHR System Uptime
P3-KPI2.note: inherits its one playbook's cost/lift figures directly; no KPI-specific override authored yet
